- The V-16 light-emitting hazard warning device or, failing this, two hazard warning triangles.
- A certified, high-visibility reflective vest inside the interior of the vehicle. It must be visible from at least 150 metres away. If the vehicle is an escort vehicle, protecting and accompanying others, vests must be worn by the driver and each member of the crew.
- A full-size spare or a temporary tyre, with the tools needed to change tyres, or an alternative system to changing them that offers sufficient guarantees for the mobility of the vehicle. In these cases, the vehicles will be driven in observance of the limitations of each alternative.
(Página 270 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Road traffic collisions
 
3 Characteristics of road collisions
Related studies that have investigated traffic collisions, show that:
In cities, the accidents that cause the most mortalities are collisions with pedestrians.
Most of the victims, especially resulting in deaths, occur on intercity routes.
Most collisions occur on the straight and not on bends.
Autopistas and autovias are generally safer than conventional roads.
Most accidents occur during public holidays (especially, Easter, summer and December).
Weekends and public festivals (bank holidays) are the most dangerous days, especially during the hours in the morning.
Most accidents occur during the daytime when people are going to or leaving work, especially at the end of the working day.
(Página 250 del manual 'Learning to drive')

5 Overtaking
5.2 General rules and exceptions
As an exception, and if there is sufficient space and implementing the maximum safety precautions an overtake must be carried out, obligatorily, to the right:
When the driver of the vehicle, which you proposed overtaking, clearly indicates their intention to change direction to the left or to stop on the left side of the roadway.
And exceptionally the hard shoulder may be used (i.e. for fluidity reasons) when there is serious congestion on the lane that flows in the opposite direction that does not permit the turn or parking on the left hand side of the roadway to be easily carried out.
(Página 186 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
ILLNESS AND MEDICATION  
   
19 The consequences of illnesses and drugs in traffic collisions
To drive a vehicle requires certain conditions relating to the physical and mental aptitude of the driver to be initially satisfied and thereafter maintained. It is therefore necessary to go to a designated medical centre for drivers who will verify whether there is a serious impediment to the applicant or driver, which will prevent them performing this task safely.
A mild illness does not have to exclude driving, although it can reduce the ability to drive safely (for example, a common cold can cause sleepiness and loss of concentration). Therefore, you should always ask your doctor about the precautions to be taken before driving, especially if you have a chronic illness.
(Página 46 del manual 'Learning to drive')
